problem: Both answers explain unsafe as 'the processes may still request resources in an order that lets them finish' / 'request and release resources in a favourable order'. That contradicts the chapter's own definition: a safe sequence is an order in which every process finishes if each takes its remaining maximum claim, so if no safe sequence exists, no request order lets all processes finish at their maxima. The standard reason an unsafe state may still escape deadlock is that processes often do not request their declared maximum (and may release held resources early), not that a finishing order exists.
fix: Q3 answer: Unsafe means no safe sequence exists, so the system cannot guarantee that every process reaches its maximum and finishes. Deadlock may still not occur, because a process may request less than its declared maximum or release resources early; the safe/unsafe test assumes the worst case, that all processes ask for their maximum. Q7 answer: No. Unsafe only says the worst case (every process asking its maximum) cannot be satisfied in any order. It is a warning, not proof; an actual deadlock needs a set of processes each waiting on a resource held by another.

problem: The last sentence says the request is refused 'if adding a claim edge would create a cycle'. A request does not add a claim edge; the claim edge already exists (drawn when the process starts) and the request converts it into a request edge. The cycle check is made when the request edge would be turned into an assignment edge.
fix: A process's future claim appears as a dashed claim edge P_i → R_j, added when the process starts and only if it keeps the graph acyclic. When P_i actually requests R_j, the claim edge becomes a request edge. The request is granted only if converting that request edge into an assignment edge R_j → P_i creates no cycle; otherwise the process waits.

problem: 'Deadlocked: a cycle of waits exists' reads as if a cycle is enough to prove deadlock. With several instances of a resource, a cycle is necessary but not sufficient, so a student can wrongly call a cyclic-but-completable state deadlocked.
fix: Deadlocked: every process in a wait cycle is blocked and no sequence of releases can free them; a deadlocked state is always unsafe. With one instance of each resource type a cycle is enough; with multiple instances a cycle is necessary but not sufficient.
